scientific_question: Why do frozen P1 Field-DPO checkpoints still fail to identify observed-consensus Label-2 answers, and which mechanisms are also present before preference optimization in frozen R3-SFT?

estimand.primary_population: seed_record occurrences with label_5 == 2 and parsed_score != 2
estimand.primary_quantity: mechanism-specific fraction of primary-population failures, reported separately by seed
not_identified: causal effects of mechanisms from observational association alone

evidence_scope.train_failure_bank_role: descriptive coverage and transition evidence only; never generalization evidence

score_probability_contract.definition: conditional sequence log-probability of each canonical score value under the identical frozen prompt and score-field prefix
score_probability_contract.normalization: softmax over the five canonical option sequence log-probabilities
score_probability_contract.decoder_prediction: parsed score from the already frozen structured generation protocol
score_probability_contract.forced_choice_prediction: argmax over normalized canonical score option probabilities

primary_exclusive_attribution.rule: first satisfied category in the frozen order; all independent flags are retained for sensitivity analysis

definitions.measurement_ambiguous: at least two valid rater scores are present and either the observed rater range is at least 2 or both boundary scores 2 and 3 occur
definitions.rubric_incomplete: two independent human reviewers agree, or adjudication concludes, that a score-decisive criterion used for the case is absent or operationally unusable in the supplied rubric
definitions.decoder_failure: the frozen parsed score is not 2 while the frozen canonical forced-choice score argmax is 2
definitions.prior_recoverable: decoder_failure is false and train-prior-neutralized frozen score probabilities have argmax 2
definitions.calibration_recoverable: decoder and prior recovery are false and the record's outer-fold prediction from nested question-group cross-fitted vector scaling has argmax 2
definitions.support_deficient: earlier rules are false, train label-2 count in the exact metric_id-language stratum is below 5, and low support has the preregistered adverse association in the adjusted occurrence-level model
definitions.preference_coverage_deficient: earlier rules are false and the frozen P1 pair graph contains no direct 2-over-3 edge for the record and no direct 2-over-3 edge in its metric_id-language stratum
definitions.residual: no earlier exclusive attribution rule is satisfied

calibration_protocol.method: multinomial vector scaling with L2 regularization
calibration_protocol.selection: inner question-group cross-validation minimizing multiclass NLL
calibration_protocol.interpretation: diagnostic recoverability, not a new model result

prior_protocol.interpretation: sensitivity test for learned class-prior attraction, not a deployment correction

support_protocol.primary_count: number of locked train rows with label_5 == 2 in the same metric_id-language stratum
support_protocol.association_model: failure indicator regressed on log1p(stratum label-2 support), metric_id, language and rater disagreement; question-cluster robust uncertainty
support_protocol.exact_question_support_is_not_used: the split is question-disjoint, so exact-question support is structurally zero

human_audit.primary_dev_records: all 14 unique dev records with label_5 == 2
human_audit.secondary_sampling_frame: train label-1/2 actual failures plus matched prediction-3 and severe-overestimate controls; no test
questions: Is score 2 uniquely defensible from the supplied rubric and answer?
Is a decisive criterion absent from the rubric?
Is a present criterion too vague to execute reproducibly?
Which evidence span determines the 2-versus-3 boundary?

statistics.gate_interpretation: project decision rule, not a universal statistical law

decision_policy.dominant_calibration_or_prior: run only matched strong calibration baselines; do not claim a new preference-learning principle
decision_policy.dominant_support: test a support-aware estimator against Balanced Softmax, class-balanced objectives and CORN before proposing a new method
decision_policy.dominant_measurement_or_rubric: treat target validity and rubric executability as the research problem before further model optimization
decision_policy.dominant_preference_coverage: derive a new estimand and a candidate-specific counterexample before implementing another preference loss
decision_policy.no_dominant_mechanism: stop CCF-A algorithm expansion and write the completed work as a rigorous master-thesis study with bounded claims
